title: Turning Point USA event held at Auburn University - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Hall ,
53 minutes ago
AUBURN, Ala. ( WIAT ) — A Turning Point USA event took place at Auburn University on Wednesday night.
U.S. Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-AL, Lara Trump, Eric Trump and Benny Johnson honored Charlie Kirk, the founder of Turning Point USA who was assassinated in Utah on Sept. 10. They spoke to students about conservative values.
Leaders were met with a raucous crowd in Neville Arena. Eric and Lara Trump spoke about family and fighting for the conservative movement.
“This is the group. This is the spirit that’s going to save the United States of America,” said Eric Trump, one of President Donald Trump’s sons. “It’s this heart. It’s this soul. It’s this movement.”
The panel took questions from students and also called the president.
“Auburn’s a special place,” Trump said on the phone. “I’ve been there many times. I know many people from that area, number one, and from that school. It’s a great school.”
Tuberville also spoke about family values and honored Kirk’s legacy.
“This is not a Republican or a Democrat issue. This is an American issue,” Tuberville said. “We don’t need to lose a country because we are not opening our eyes. And here tonight, we’re trying to open the eyes of a lot of young people that might vote for something that they would regret later.”
Who is Nick Fuentes? At one point, the far-right provocateur considered making his home in Alabama Before the event, students shared their thoughts on what the Turning Point USA event means to them. Ian Gunn, president of the College Democrats at Auburn, said these events can cause controversy.
“I think honoring your founding member … is something that should be enshrined in the principles of free speech. There’s nothing wrong with that,” Gunn said. “However, I do think that we do have to acknowledge in some ways that he was a controversial character.”
Ty Torbert, vice chairman of the College Republicans at Auburn, said civil discourse is important.
“We need not only conservative leadership, we need young conservative leadership,” Torbert said, “to bring in this new era, this new generation of thinking, to push our country forward and stop looking back towards the past.”
Torbert said he hopes both sides were able to engage in that civil discourse at Wednesday’s event.
